title: Best Anime Streaming in India
intro: Anime's Indian streaming footprint is bigger than most people realise - Netflix alone carries a library that would have required a grey-market importer a decade ago. These are the series worth your bandwidth, whether you've been watching since Doordarshan aired Dragon Ball Z or you're arriving fresh off the Demon Slayer train.

picks.title: Attack on Titan
picks.one_line: A siege-war epic that starts as survival horror and ends as one of the most morally complex political dramas in any medium this decade.

picks.title: Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood
picks.one_line: The benchmark for long-form anime storytelling - a war-and-alchemy saga with zero filler and a finale that earns every minute of its 64 episodes.

picks.title: Death Note
picks.one_line: A cat-and-mouse chess match between a genius mass murderer and a prodigy detective - 37 episodes of pure psychological tension, no filler.

picks.title: Demon Slayer
picks.one_line: The best-looking shonen on Netflix India right now: Ufotable's animation is a theatrical experience compressed into episode runtimes.

picks.title: Vinland Saga
picks.one_line: A Viking revenge saga that halfway through dismantles itself and becomes something far more profound - the anime equivalent of early Game of Thrones with actual follow-through.

picks.title: Spy x Family
picks.one_line: A Cold War spy is forced to build a fake family - the show is endlessly charming, and Anya is the best comedy character of this generation.

picks.title: Hunter x Hunter
picks.one_line: Starts as a classic shonen adventure and peaks with the Chimera Ant arc - a 30-episode sequence that belongs in the same breath as the best prestige TV.

picks.title: Neon Genesis Evangelion
picks.one_line: The mecha genre's detonation point - a show about giant robots that is actually about depression, and has not aged a day in its psychological horror.

faq.q: Where is the best place to stream anime in India?
faq.a: Netflix carries the highest-profile titles (Attack on Titan, Death Note, Evangelion, Demon Slayer). Prime Video has Vinland Saga and a few exclusives. Crunchyroll is the deepest catalogue for seasonal anime and back-catalogue classics like FMA Brotherhood and Hunter x Hunter - worth the subscription if you watch more than two shows a month.

faq.q: Which anime should an absolute beginner start with?
faq.a: Death Note is the cleanest gateway - 37 episodes, no prior context required, and it hooks within two episodes. Once that's done, Attack on Titan for scale and Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood for pure craft. Avoid starting with Naruto or One Piece until you know you're committed; the episode counts are brutal.
